body:
A work run on task:da797576d0cfaaac lost the Solace tool for the rest of its run (run `d0f587f579672c1b`, step 34). The agent sent a batch whose first line was only `--project solace-cli/board`. `run_options` strips `--project <dir>`, which leaves no words, and then indexes `a[0]` (the `extract`/`merge` check in a board run). That panics, and the MCP server process dies because nothing in the `tools/call` loop catches a panic. Every later call got `Transport closed`, and the run ended as "agent exited without finishing".

- **Empty command:** in `batch`, a line that has no verb once `--project <dir>` is removed is refused as that line's error: "`--project` goes on the same line as its command, e.g. `view x.y --project <dir>`". The rest of the batch runs as usual.
- **Panic guard:** each `tools/call` runs inside `catch_unwind`. A panic becomes an error reply ("Solace hit an internal error running `<line>`: <panic message>; nothing after it ran"), and the server keeps serving. Per-call thread-local state (`SHOWN`, `COMMAND_DB`, `UNTESTED`) is reset before the next call. Any open transaction is rolled back, so no half-done change is kept.
- Tests: a batch with a `--project`-only line replies with the refusal, and the next line still runs. A forced panic in a command returns an error, and the next call succeeds.

Out of scope: auditing other `a[0]` indexing (the guard covers it); having the board notice a dead MCP server and say so in the run outcome.
title: MCP: survive a bad command line
